name: drift-x
concept: A slow, small, continuous horizontal drift instead of a vertical bob. Use it for an idle element on a horizontal layout, like a list item or a side panel icon.

name: drift-x-wide
concept: A horizontal drift that lingers at its furthest point before returning. Use it when an idle element should pause and feel unhurried, not just oscillate.

name: creep-x
concept: A small horizontal creep that pauses, then eases back past its start before it settles. Use it for an idle element that should feel like it slowly explores its space.

name: drift-x-tilt
concept: A tiny horizontal drift paired with a very small rotation. Use it for an idle element that should feel loose and slightly playful, not rigid.

name: pendulum-drift
concept: An asymmetric horizontal swing that travels further one way than the other, like a pendulum that loses energy. Use it for an idle element that should feel like it settles, not perfectly balanced.

name: drift-x-flicker
concept: A small horizontal drift paired with a very faint opacity dip at its peak. Use it for an idle element that should feel subtly alive, like a soft flicker of attention.

name: float-diagonal
concept: A small float that moves on a diagonal path instead of straight up. Use it for an idle illustration or icon that should feel like it drifts freely, not on one axis.

name: float-diagonal-reverse
concept: A small diagonal float toward the opposite corner, down and to the left. Use it to vary the direction of idle motion across a set of floating elements.

name: float-diagonal-zigzag
concept: A small float that arcs from one side to the other while it rises, like a gentle zigzag. Use it for an idle element that should feel like it traces a soft path.

name: float-diagonal-tilt
concept: A small diagonal float paired with a very slight lean. Use it for an idle element that should feel like it gently leans into its own motion.

name: float-diagonal-quick
concept: A diagonal float that moves out quickly, then eases back slowly. Use it for an idle element that should feel like it darts gently, then rests.

name: float-diagonal-triangle
concept: A small float that visits three points in a loose triangular path. Use it for an idle element that should feel like it wanders gently, not just back and forth.

name: float-breathe
concept: A small vertical float combined with a very subtle scale pulse. Use it for an idle element that should feel calm, alive, and gently expanding as it rises.

name: float-swell
concept: A float where the scale pulse peaks slightly before the vertical rise. Use it for an idle element that should feel like it swells first, then lifts.

name: float-pulse-soft
concept: A gentle float combined with a very faint scale and opacity pulse. Use it for an idle element that should feel softly alive without it drawing attention.

name: float-grow
phrase: float and grow on the rise
concept: A float where the scale grows only while the element rises, then shrinks back as it falls. Use it for an idle element that should feel like it gathers energy on the way up.

name: float-breathe-wide
concept: A wide, slow float and breathe cycle with a gentle build and release. Use it for an idle element that should feel unhurried and calm over a longer cycle.

name: float-breathe-tilt
concept: A float and breathe cycle with a very slight rotation added. Use it for an idle element that should feel gently alive and slightly loose.

name: float-quick-rise
concept: A float that rises quickly, then eases back down slowly. Use it for an idle element that should feel like it lifts with a little energy, then rests gently.

name: float-quick-fall
concept: A float that rises slowly, then drops back down quickly. Use it for an idle element that should feel like it gathers gently, then releases with a small snap.

name: float-snap-up
concept: A float that snaps upward quickly, holds briefly, then drifts back down slowly. Use it for an idle element that should feel like it perks up now and then.

name: float-overshoot-settle
concept: A float that rises slightly past its resting point, then eases back to settle. Use it for an idle element that should feel like it gently overshoots before it rests.

name: float-lag
concept: A float that stays near rest for most of its cycle, then drops and returns quickly near the end. Use it for an idle element that should feel mostly still with an occasional small dip.

name: suspend
concept: An extremely slow, extremely small vertical drift that feels almost still. Use it for an idle element that should feel suspended in place, calmer than a float.

name: suspend-deep
concept: An even smaller vertical drift paired with a barely visible opacity shift. Use it for an idle element that should feel deeply calm and nearly motionless.

name: suspend-tilt
concept: An extremely slow, extremely small rotation instead of a vertical drift. Use it for an idle element that should feel suspended with the faintest hint of turning.

name: suspend-scale
concept: A scale pulse so small and so slow it stays near rest for most of its cycle. Use it for an idle element that should feel like the quietest possible sign of life.

name: suspend-drift
concept: An extremely slow, extremely small diagonal drift. Use it for an idle element that should feel suspended but with the faintest sense of direction.

name: breathe-slow-grow
concept: A breathe pulse that grows slowly, then shrinks back quickly. Use it for an idle element that should feel like it gathers gently, then releases with a small snap.

name: breathe-quick-grow
concept: A breathe pulse that grows quickly, then shrinks back slowly. Use it for an idle element that should feel like it perks up, then settles gently.

name: breathe-hold
concept: A breathe pulse that grows, holds briefly at its peak, then shrinks back. Use it for an idle element that should feel like it pauses at full attention.

name: breathe-swell-deep
concept: A deeper breathe pulse that swells quickly, then eases down slowly over most of the cycle. Use it for an idle element that should feel like a stronger, still-subtle sign of life.

name: breathe-flutter
concept: A breathe pulse with two small peaks of different heights in one cycle. Use it for an idle element that should feel like a soft double breath, not a single pulse.

name: breathe-float
concept: A breathe pulse with a small vertical float that moves in step. Use it for an idle element where the pulse should lead and the float should feel secondary.

name: breathe-float-offset
concept: A breathe pulse and a small float that peak at slightly different moments. Use it for an idle element that should feel like its pulse and lift are gently out of step.

name: breathe-float-micro
concept: An extremely tiny combined scale and vertical float, almost imperceptible. Use it for an idle element that should feel alive at the smallest possible scale.

name: breathe-float-deep
concept: A slower, slightly larger combined scale and float cycle. Use it for an idle element that should feel calm but with a bit more presence than the micro version.

name: breathe-float-fast
concept: A quicker combined scale and float cycle with a held middle stage. Use it for an idle element that should feel briskly alive, not sluggish.

name: breathe-float-hold
concept: A combined scale and float that holds briefly at its peak before it returns. Use it for an idle element that should feel like it pauses gently at full lift.

name: hover-idle
concept: A tiny, fast vertical jitter. Use it for an element that should feel live and idle, like it hovers in place, rather than static.

name: hover-idle-double
concept: A tiny vertical jitter with two small beats per cycle instead of one. Use it for an idle element that should feel like it has a quick pulse of life, twice as often.

name: hover-flicker
concept: A tiny vertical jitter paired with a very faint opacity dip. Use it for an idle element that should feel live, like a soft flicker of activity.

name: hover-tick
concept: A tiny vertical jitter that snaps between two close positions with brief holds. Use it for an idle element that should feel like a small mechanical tick, not a smooth bob.

name: hover-tremble
concept: A tiny tremor that moves in both horizontal and vertical directions at once. Use it for an idle element that should feel like it has a faint, live tremble.

name: hover-idle-scale
concept: A tiny vertical jitter paired with a barely visible scale flicker. Use it for an idle element that should feel live through both motion and the faintest pulse.

name: orbit-drift-quarter
concept: A small circular drift traced through four quarter-phase points. Use it for an idle element that should feel like it gently orbits in place.

name: orbit-drift-reverse
concept: The same small circular drift traced in the opposite rotational direction. Use it to vary the orbit direction across a set of idle elements.

name: orbit-drift-wide
concept: A small elliptical drift that is wider side to side than top to bottom. Use it for an idle element that should feel like it traces a gentle, flattened orbit.

name: orbit-drift-tight
phrase: drift in a tight pulse orbit
concept: A small circular drift with a faint scale pulse at the far points of the loop. Use it for an idle element that should feel like it breathes as it orbits.

name: orbit-drift-slow
phrase: drift in a slow tall ellipse
concept: A slow elliptical drift that is taller top to bottom than side to side. Use it for an idle element that should feel like a gentle, vertical-leaning orbit.
